current_vanilla_pressure: Iron feeds tools, hoppers, rails, anvils, armour, and many automation builds. Early mining is finite and slow compared with late demand.
common_optimal_farm: Iron golem farm, often combined with a trading hall.
why_players_feel_forced: The same material is needed for both basic infrastructure and high-volume automation, while a correct farm runs unattended and outperforms ordinary mining.
matcha_behavior: Observed recipes and trades use iron for tools, rails, anvil, hopper, and an iron-ingot-from-iron-materials conversion. Vanilla-namespace item definitions also exist. No iron-farm rule is established by the static audit. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, registry-data.json, assets.json. Runtime throughput is UNKNOWN. Check a disposable-server rate trace and farm interaction test.
active_route: Mining, salvage, and deliberate quarry work remain useful for the first stock and for players who enjoy active extraction.
civic_route: A registered mine, smithy, or settlement recycling service can fulfil declared iron demand with workers and storage.
technical_route: An engineered farm or smelter may reach high throughput, but it needs real inputs, infrastructure, mob management, and bounded output handling.
trade_route: Smiths, merchants, or freight routes can import iron against a real order rather than an abstract infinite balance.
discovery_route: Ore exposure, ruins, and regional geology can teach safe extraction and processing without granting a permanent multiplier.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Saturate at bounded storage or declared demand. Unattended output should lose value sharply once receiving capacity is full.
nerf_needed: No blanket nerf before repair, rail, and project supply alternatives are measured. Revisit only if the farm still dominates after those routes exist.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla farms are available. Technical production mods are provisional and none is selected for 26.2 yet.
custom_work_required: Define shared demand, warehouse, and output-cap rules without replacing every farm with custom Java.
open_questions: What iron-per-hour target makes mining, civic supply, and engineering comparably sensible for different project scales?

current_vanilla_pressure: Experience levels pay for enchanting, anvil work, and often modded progression. Vanilla farms turn the general-purpose currency into a bankable commodity.
common_optimal_farm: Mob grinder, gold farm, furnace XP bank, or villager trading loop.
why_players_feel_forced: Many unrelated systems consume the same resource, so an XP farm becomes a prerequisite even for players who dislike combat or redstone engineering.
matcha_behavior: Observed scoreboard objective anvil_interaction and functions that set a player to 100 levels, then remove levels and points outside an exclusion tag. This is classified as an override. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/functions.json, scoreboards.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv. Exact timing and selector scope are UNKNOWN without a runtime trace. Check two-player, restart, and vanilla-control traces.
active_route: Meaningful exploration, first-time discoveries, completed projects, and demonstrated technique provide progression evidence without raw action volume.
civic_route: Training, workshops, and civic projects can reward knowledge or service access instead of forcing every player to bank XP.
technical_route: XP farms remain a first-class engineering option when their inputs, storage, and demand are explicit, but AFK accumulation must saturate.
trade_route: Repair, training, and commissions can use visible service costs. A fee should not silently become a second XP farm.
discovery_route: Learning a new recipe, route, or technique can award a bounded first-understanding milestone.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive XP storage or conversion and make long unattended sessions sharply less valuable.
nerf_needed: Do not remove vanilla XP before alternative repair and progression routes work. The Matcha XP override itself needs narrow replacement or disablement because it can erase XP.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla farms and furnace banking exist. No selected cross-mod XP support is verified for 26.2.
custom_work_required: Separate Forever mastery evidence from player XP, then adapt Matcha through stable concepts rather than importing its scoreboard semantics.
open_questions: Should XP remain a vanilla resource alongside evidence-based mastery, and which services may consume it after repair is available?

current_vanilla_pressure: Mending collapses replacement and repair costs into a single enchantment when paired with a renewable XP source.
common_optimal_farm: Librarian trading hall, loot search, or villager rerolling.
why_players_feel_forced: A player who wants durable tools is pushed towards villager infrastructure and XP production before they can enjoy the work they actually value.
matcha_behavior: Observed blessings:mending recipe and hell_bound_book recipe-unlock path. The enchanting-table tag has replace=true and the archive contains 23 blessing recipes. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, advancements.json, tags.json; runtime availability and final cost are UNKNOWN. Check recipe unlock, enchanting-table, anvil, and trade traces.
active_route: Field repair kits and expedition salvage keep a trip viable without requiring the enchantment.
civic_route: Workshops and smiths provide full repair through materials, time, or a service contract.
technical_route: A bounded repair station can automate handling only with real repair inputs and atomic transactions.
trade_route: Librarians, smiths, and merchants may sell a repair service or a known book, not an unlimited free durability loop.
discovery_route: First learning of a repair technique can explain the process and unlock a route without making Mending the only answer.
passive_output_cap_needed: No direct passive output. Cap repair throughput by materials, service slots, and demand rather than by item deletion.
nerf_needed: No blanket removal before the field, workshop, and economic routes are usable. Classify or disable the Matcha blessing path only after a compatibility decision.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla anvil and Matcha blessing recipes are present. Repair-service mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Resolve precedence between vanilla Mending, Matcha blessings, and Forever equipment repair while preserving named item identity.
open_questions: Should Mending remain a scarce convenience, a translated repair technique, or an optional route that never bypasses repair costs?

current_vanilla_pressure: A Totem of Undying converts a rare danger buffer into a renewable safety stock when raids are farmed.
common_optimal_farm: Raid farm or repeated evoker kills.
why_players_feel_forced: High-risk exploration feels incomplete without a stockpile because one farm can turn an exceptional rescue into routine equipment.
matcha_behavior: UNKNOWN: the audit contains three totem references across generated reports but no dedicated reviewed totem classification. Check generated/matcha/1.12/loot-tables.json, registry-data.json, functions.json, and a disposable runtime trace for acquisition, use, and repeatability.
active_route: Dangerous structures, bosses, and expeditions can provide limited first access and meaningful risk.
civic_route: Sanctuaries, rescue services, safer routes, and prepared shelters reduce the need for a consumable death override without removing danger.
technical_route: Raid farms remain a legitimate engineering route, but encounter rates and output need bounded demand and no infinite stacking benefit.
trade_route: A steward can sell rescue preparation, route insurance, or a limited totem supply with visible scarcity.
discovery_route: A first structure or encounter can teach the protection's existence without turning every expedition into a checklist.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Bound passive stock by storage or expected demand. Do not award permanent defensive percentages from repeated structures.
nerf_needed: No direct nerf until alternative safety and recovery routes are tested. If supply remains dominant, adjust encounter economics rather than deleting the established playstyle.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla raid farms are available. No additional 26.2 support is verified.
custom_work_required: Add adventure-instance claims, safe recovery, and explicit protection rules only after Matcha totem evidence is traced.
open_questions: Is the Matcha reference a normal item, a disguised identity, or a structure reward, and how should it coexist with heirloom recovery?

current_vanilla_pressure: Gunpowder is consumed by rockets, TNT, fire charges, and several technical recipes. Its value is tied to mobility and large-scale excavation.
common_optimal_farm: Creeper farm, witch farm, or general hostile mob farm.
why_players_feel_forced: Rocket travel and explosive projects create continuous demand, while a creeper farm supplies it unattended at a scale active hunting cannot match.
matcha_behavior: Observed gunpowder references in ore and chest loot, plus sulfur conversion recipes and recipes for fire charge, TNT, benzene, phosphor, and dyes. No farm suppression is established; farm behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check loot and farm traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, loot-tables.json, functions.json.
active_route: Creeper hunting, structure exploration, and mining provide active early supply.
civic_route: A chemical works or explosives guild can handle declared project demand with safe storage and licensing.
technical_route: Creeper farms remain first-class engineering, but rates, storage, and rocket demand must be bounded.
trade_route: Gunpowder or processed sulfur can be traded and shipped from a known source.
discovery_route: Finding sulfur, hostile habitats, or an explosives technique can open options without requiring a farm.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Bound unattended gunpowder by receiving capacity and rocket or project demand.
nerf_needed: Potential narrow travel rebalance only after rail, ports, and bedroll routes work. Do not ban creeper farms as a first response.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla hostile farms and Matcha sulfur-related recipes are present. Technical production candidates are provisional.
custom_work_required: Make rocket consumption, explosive safety, and passive caps data-driven while preserving normal combat and mining.
open_questions: What rocket and TNT demand should count as healthy engineering throughput rather than mandatory flight upkeep?

current_vanilla_pressure: Firework rockets make Elytra the fastest answer to most long-distance travel and consume gunpowder and sugarcane at scale.
common_optimal_farm: Creeper farm plus sugarcane farm, often with a shulker transport loop.
why_players_feel_forced: Without an equally reliable repeated-route service, players rush the End, Elytra, and two farms before building the world they want.
matcha_behavior: UNKNOWN: generated reports record Elytra advancements, recipes, and resource assets, but no static rule establishes the final rocket-flight relationship. Check generated/matcha/1.12/functions.json, recipes.json, assets.json, and a disposable runtime flight trace.
active_route: Walking, horses, boats, gliding, and first-trip exploration remain valid. Rockets support difficult crossings rather than every commute.
civic_route: Roads, passenger rail, ports, and established services make fixed routes better than personal flight.
technical_route: Rocket production remains a high-throughput technical route with real sugarcane, gunpowder, storage, and handling costs.
trade_route: Rocket supply can be bought, while fares for a route service offer a non-flight economic alternative.
discovery_route: The first Elytra or glider discovery can unlock scouting without making rockets the mandatory artifact rush.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes for sugarcane and gunpowder inputs. Inventory caps alone are not enough; demand saturation and diminishing unattended value are also needed.
nerf_needed: A narrow travel-balance intervention is already the subject of ADR 0013. Do not apply it until rail and other fixed-route alternatives are usable and measured.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla rockets are available. Rail, boat, and flight-adjacent mods are provisional for 26.2.
custom_work_required: Integrate travel services, rocket policy, and route validation without making the client decide movement outcomes.
open_questions: What fixed-route service time and capacity reliably beat flight without making exploration feel slow?

current_vanilla_pressure: Stone, cobblestone, deepslate, and variants are consumed by ordinary building, roads, furnaces, and civic projects at enormous volume.
common_optimal_farm: Cobblestone or stone generator, quarry, TNT quarry, or mining beacon.
why_players_feel_forced: The material is common but project quantities are huge. A generator saves enough labour that builders feel required to construct one before starting a major design.
matcha_behavior: Observed blasting recipes convert stone, smooth stone, stone bricks, and mossy variants, and mason trade records include stone families. No passive stone-generator rule is established; runtime farm interaction is UNKNOWN. Check generator, processing, and storage traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, registry-data.json, loot-tables.json.
active_route: Mining, quarrying, and terrain reuse remain satisfying active routes.
civic_route: A registered quarry, stoneworks, or settlement order converts physical extraction into a predictable civic supply.
technical_route: Generators and processing lines may reach high throughput with real fuel, space, wear, design, and output handling.
trade_route: Masons and carriers can sell or import common stone against project demand.
discovery_route: A discovered strata, quarry, or ruin can teach material families and useful processing.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Saturate at warehouse capacity or project demand, with no value for unhandled overflow.
nerf_needed: No stone-generator nerf before civic supply, building assistance, and trade routes are usable. Reassess dominance with project-scale tests.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla generators and Matcha processing recipes are available. Create-style production is provisional.
custom_work_required: Define project demand and storage caps without making the server simulate every block in a quarry.
open_questions: What project sizes and delivery times should set the parity target for mining, civic quarrying, and engineering?

current_vanilla_pressure: Wood is a universal input for tools, fuel, chests, rails, buildings, and early infrastructure. Replanting does not remove the repetitive harvest pressure.
common_optimal_farm: Large tree farm, TNT tree farm, or manually optimised plantation.
why_players_feel_forced: Every path consumes wood, and a high-throughput farm removes the labour cost while still allowing unlimited stockpiles.
matcha_behavior: Observed wood references and extensive log trade records exist, but no wood-growth or farm-control mechanic is established in the static audit. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, registry-data.json, cross-references.json. Growth behaviour is UNKNOWN.
active_route: Manual forestry, varied species harvesting, and landscape stewardship remain valid.
civic_route: A managed woodland, forester, or settlement timber yard supplies declared needs and replaces wasteful repeated trips.
technical_route: Tree farms remain first-class when they require space, saplings, time, and output handling. AFK overflow has no value.
trade_route: Timber can be commissioned or shipped from a known forest with species and quality visible.
discovery_route: The first forest or species discovery can add regional identity and knowledge.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive output at storage or demand and make unhandled logs worthless rather than endlessly accumulating.
nerf_needed: No blanket tree-farm nerf before managed woodland, trade, and freight alternatives exist.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla farms and Matcha log trade records are available. Forestry mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Add species-aware supply tags and bounded output without forcing a custom tree simulation.
open_questions: How should rare species retain regional value after a player establishes a sustainable local source?

current_vanilla_pressure: Sand feeds glass, concrete, sandstone, bottles, and explosives. Vanilla supply is geographically concentrated and duplication has historically been attractive.
common_optimal_farm: Desert quarry, gravel conversion, or a sand duplication machine.
why_players_feel_forced: Large glass and concrete projects consume thousands of blocks, while normal digging damages a region and engineered duplication feels mandatory for scale.
matcha_behavior: Observed recipes include sand from blasting gravel, quartz from blasting sand, red sand from sand and iron, and multiple sand-related loot references. No duplication rule is established; duplication behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check duplication and output-saturation traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, loot-tables.json, advancements.json.
active_route: Desert, river, and badlands extraction remain valid first supplies and exploration targets.
civic_route: A registered glassworks or quarry can fulfil project orders while making landscape impact and stock visible.
technical_route: Conversion and duplication may be engineered, but throughput requires inputs, infrastructure, storage, and explicit output handling.
trade_route: Sand and glass can be imported from a known region or purchased from a mason or carrier.
discovery_route: A first desert or badlands discovery can teach source, colour, and processing options.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive or duplicated output at bounded storage and live demand. Long AFK sessions should saturate quickly.
nerf_needed: Do not remove duplication or mass mining before a satisfying glass and concrete supply exists. If needed, target unbounded output handling rather than all technical play.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla smelting and Matcha conversion recipes are available. Processing mods are provisional for 26.2.
custom_work_required: Define region impact, supply caps, and project demand without requiring world-wide sand scans.
open_questions: Can a quarry, glassworks, or trade route meet mega-build demand without making a desert disposable?

current_vanilla_pressure: Gravel is needed for concrete, flint, paths, and sand conversion. It is awkward to gather at project scale and often becomes a by-product problem.
common_optimal_farm: Gravel mining, piglin bartering, or duplication.
why_players_feel_forced: It is easy to need a large quantity and unpleasant to collect manually, while the same infrastructure can produce sand or flint.
matcha_behavior: Observed gravel block loot and a blasting recipe converting cobbled materials to gravel. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/loot-tables.json, recipes.json, advancements.json. No farm-specific behaviour is established; runtime farm behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check mining, bartering, and conversion traces.
active_route: Riverbed, mountain, and underground extraction provide active supply.
civic_route: A quarry or aggregate works can combine gravel, flint, sand, and concrete orders.
technical_route: A crusher or generator can scale only with real inputs, fuel, space, and output handling.
trade_route: Aggregate can be purchased or moved with a physical freight order.
discovery_route: Finding a gravelly biome or learning the conversion route adds useful regional knowledge.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap aggregate overflow at storage or demand; stop crediting production once buffers are full.
nerf_needed: No direct nerf before aggregate works and sand/glass routes are available. Preserve bartering and active mining.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla mining, bartering, and Matcha blasting recipe are available. Crusher mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Unify aggregate demand and prevent conversion chains from becoming hidden infinite loops.
open_questions: Should gravel-to-sand conversion be a low-efficiency safety valve, a specialist process, or both?

current_vanilla_pressure: Clay supports bricks, terracotta, pottery, mud construction, and decorative projects. Large palette builds exhaust local deposits.
common_optimal_farm: Mud-to-clay or dripstone clay farm, river excavation, or trading.
why_players_feel_forced: Aesthetic building needs clay in bulk, but manual collection is slow and biome-specific, so a farm becomes preparation rather than a creative choice.
matcha_behavior: Observed recipes include clay from mud and potion and clay balls from clay, plus archaeology and clay statue records. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, advancements.json, loot-tables.json. No growth or farm rule is established; runtime growth and farm behaviour are UNKNOWN. Check mud, dripstone, and crop traces.
active_route: River, swamp, and archaeology gathering remain valid active routes.
civic_route: A brickworks, pottery, or mason service can turn a declared clay demand into local stock.
technical_route: Mud, water, dripstone, and processing systems may be engineered with bounded inputs and storage.
trade_route: Clay, terracotta, or finished masonry can be traded or shipped.
discovery_route: A first wetland, ruin, or pottery practice can reveal material families and safe processing.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Saturate at storage or active project demand; never build an unbounded hidden reserve.
nerf_needed: No clay-farm nerf before brickworks, trade, and project supply alternatives exist.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla mud/dripstone routes and Matcha clay recipes are available. Pottery mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Define substitutions and regional supply without making a required aesthetic or architecture style.
open_questions: How should rare terracotta colours and local clay remain meaningful after home production is established?

current_vanilla_pressure: Glass and panes are consumed by windows, bottles, stations, and many decorative or technical builds. The input chain inherits sand pressure.
common_optimal_farm: Automated furnace array fed by a sand quarry or duplication machine.
why_players_feel_forced: Glass is fragile to place manually and appears in large counts, so players feel compelled to industrialise before building.
matcha_behavior: Observed glass recipes, glass bottle recipes, glass-pane unlocks, and food recipes returning bottles. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, advancements.json, assets.json. No special glass production rule is established; runtime production is UNKNOWN. Check furnace, processing, and automated-output traces.
active_route: Manual smelting and small glassworks remain useful for early homes and prototypes.
civic_route: A civic glassworks can fulfil project orders, recycle declared inputs, and provide a local service.
technical_route: Furnace arrays and processing lines remain a first-class engineering route when fuel, sand, storage, and output handling are real.
trade_route: Glassmakers can sell or ship panes, bottles, and other finished goods.
discovery_route: A desert, ruin, or old glassworks can reveal recipes and regional palette options.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap automated output by receiving capacity and active demand, not by making furnaces slow for everyone.
nerf_needed: Do not nerf glass processing independently of sand alternatives. First make civic works and trade genuinely usable.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla smelting and Matcha recipe extensions are available. Processing mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Provide recipe-viewer explanations and safe handling of fragile outputs without changing ordinary glass placement.
open_questions: What output buffer and project-order model makes a glassworks valuable without becoming a required factory?

current_vanilla_pressure: Slimeballs power pistons, leads, sticky blocks, and technical construction. Supply is location- and spawn-dependent.
common_optimal_farm: Slime-chunk farm, swamp farm, or Nether portal farm.
why_players_feel_forced: Redstone projects can stop entirely without slime, and locating a viable farm is opaque enough that players often use a guide or a large technical build.
matcha_behavior: Observed recipes include vanilla slime ball from slime block and a Matcha slime-ball recipe using lime dye and a shulker spawn-egg signature. A slime tag and loot references exist, but no slime spawn balance is established. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, tags.json, loot-tables.json. Runtime identity handling is UNKNOWN. Check the exact signature, spawn, and recipe runtime traces.
active_route: Swamp exploration, slime hunting, and salvaging slime blocks provide active routes.
civic_route: A technical workshop or settlement stockroom can prepare redstone orders from declared slime supply.
technical_route: Slime farms remain first-class, but spawning, output, and storage must be bounded and not feed recursive duplication chains.
trade_route: Slimeballs and finished components can be traded or shipped after a source is known.
discovery_route: Discovering a swamp, slime chunk, or safe processing recipe can reveal the possibility without demanding a farm immediately.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive slime output at storage or technical demand, with no value for overflow.
nerf_needed: No spawn nerf before alternate discovery, trade, and workshop supply exist. Avoid touching farms to solve an information problem.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla slime routes and Matcha slime recipes are available. Technical alternatives are provisional.
custom_work_required: Audit disguised inputs exactly and keep unknown signatures on the vanilla-safe path.
open_questions: Does the Matcha slime recipe represent an intentional alternate route or a disguised identity that must be disabled?

current_vanilla_pressure: Prismarine, crystals, and sea lanterns are tied to ocean monuments and large decorative or lighting builds.
common_optimal_farm: Guardian farm, ocean monument clearing, or monument trading.
why_players_feel_forced: A single structure supplies both rare building blocks and a technical light source, so builders are pushed into a hostile farm before they can use the palette.
matcha_behavior: Observed prismarine, dark prismarine, prismarine-brick, and sea-lantern recipes, plus prismarine-shard-to-crystals processing and alloy recipes. No guardian spawn rule is established; guardian output behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check monument, guardian, and farm output traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, advancements.json, loot-tables.json.
active_route: Ocean exploration, monument clearing, and salvaged blocks supply the first stock.
civic_route: A coastal works or mason can process monument materials into a declared local order.
technical_route: Guardian farms remain a strong engineering route with real build, spawn, and output-handling costs.
trade_route: Prismarine blocks, crystals, or finished lights can be traded and shipped from coastal regions.
discovery_route: The first monument or warm-ocean discovery can unlock a palette and a technique without requiring repeat farming.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive guardian output by demand and storage. Do not let monument bonuses stack infinitely.
nerf_needed: No guardian-farm nerf before coastal trade and masonry alternatives exist. Preserve technical mastery as a valid route.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla monuments and Matcha processing recipes are available. Ocean and masonry mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Define a bounded structural reward and avoid making one rare structure the only source of all coastal building capability.
open_questions: How much prismarine should a first monument provide before a farm becomes the efficient but optional specialist path?

current_vanilla_pressure: Gold feeds powered rails, redstone timing, barter, clocks, equipment, and high-value food. Nether farms create enormous surplus.
common_optimal_farm: Zombified piglin or Nether gold farm, sometimes paired with bartering.
why_players_feel_forced: Gold is both a technical input and a currency-adjacent material, while a farm can produce more than ordinary projects consume.
matcha_behavior: Observed raw-gold-to-ingot and golden equipment recipes, powered-rail recipes, and many gold loot references. Matcha difficulty functions set drop_chances for piglins and zombified piglins, but final gold output is UNKNOWN without runtime tests. Check piglin drops, farm rates, and Matcha precedence. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, loot-tables.json, functions.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv.
active_route: Mining, Nether expeditions, and treasure remain active sources.
civic_route: A railworks, mint, or settlement works can consume gold against declared routes or projects.
technical_route: Gold farms remain first-class engineering, but bartering, rail demand, and storage must saturate rather than reward infinite AFK.
trade_route: Gold can be traded, shipped, or exchanged for services with a separate Obol policy.
discovery_route: Nether geology, bastions, and piglin practices can introduce gold and barter knowledge.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Bound passive gold by storage, barter demand, and rail/project orders.
nerf_needed: No blanket gold-farm nerf before rail and economic sinks are usable. Test the Matcha drop override separately from vanilla farm balance.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla farms, Matcha gold recipes, and piglin-related functions are present. Tech and rail mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Keep gold material identity separate from Obol currency and audit Matcha drop changes behind the adapter.
open_questions: Which gold sinks are useful enough to absorb output without inventing a mandatory luxury market?

current_vanilla_pressure: Copper serves building, oxidation, tools, wiring, and technical components. Its many forms create processing and storage pressure rather than one simple farm.
common_optimal_farm: Drowned farm, raw-copper mining, or a copper processing line.
why_players_feel_forced: Players need large quantities for both aesthetics and machinery, while oxidation variants and tool recipes multiply the stock decisions.
matcha_behavior: Observed extensive copper content: 151 recipes, 211 asset records, copper tools, patina recipes, and copper-wire/redstone recipes. Many definitions occupy the vanilla namespace, creating high identity and compatibility risk. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, assets.json, cross-references.json, vanilla-overrides.csv, system-classification.csv. Farm throughput and oxidation behaviour are UNKNOWN. Check drowned rates, processing, and oxidation traces.
active_route: Mining and planned oxidation provide active, visually meaningful supply.
civic_route: A copperworks can manage oxidation, building orders, and recycling for a settlement.
technical_route: Drowned farms and processing lines remain first-class with real spawn, energy, storage, and output handling.
trade_route: Copper forms and finished components can be commissioned or shipped from a works.
discovery_route: A first vein, ruin, or patina technique can reveal the material family and processing choices.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive output by active orders and bounded storage, especially for duplicate oxidation states.
nerf_needed: Do not nerf copper farms before building and technical alternatives are tested. Prioritise identity conflict and output saturation over blanket scarcity.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla copper and extensive Matcha recipes are present. Copper-processing mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Use exact Matcha signatures and preserve ordinary copper when the profile or resource pack is absent.
open_questions: Should oxidation be time-based, service-based, or both, and how will a works avoid becoming mandatory for decorative builds?

current_vanilla_pressure: Nether quartz supports redstone components, comparators, observers, clocks, and pale construction palettes. It requires repeated Nether travel or bartering.
common_optimal_farm: Nether quartz mining, piglin bartering, or a quarry with Fortune.
why_players_feel_forced: Technical builds consume quartz in batches and ordinary mining is exposed to danger, so players feel pushed to a dedicated Nether route or farm.
matcha_behavior: Observed quartz from Nether-quartz and lapis-related loot references, plus a recipe converting sand to quartz by blasting. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, loot-tables.json, advancements.json. No quartz-farm override is established; farm override and runtime conversion behaviour are UNKNOWN. Check sand conversion, quartz mining, and bartering traces.
active_route: Nether mining, bastion exploration, and active bartering remain meaningful.
civic_route: A redstone works or mason can process quartz into declared local orders.
technical_route: Mining or bartering automation remains valid with real travel, inputs, risk, storage, and output handling.
trade_route: Quartz and finished redstone parts can be traded or shipped.
discovery_route: A first Nether region or processing discovery can reveal a renewable alternative without requiring a farm.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Saturate unattended quartz at storage or technical demand.
nerf_needed: No quartz-farm nerf before redstone works and trade alternatives exist. Preserve both mining and bartering.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla Nether routes and Matcha quartz processing are available. Redstone/processing mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Ensure the alternate sand-to-quartz recipe does not become an unbounded conversion loop and expose its inputs clearly.
open_questions: Should sand-to-quartz be a specialist rescue route, a trade input, or a normal late-game process?

current_vanilla_pressure: Food creates continuous hunger, saturation, healing, and travel pressure. Vanilla farms make one food choice dominate because it is cheap and stackable.
common_optimal_farm: Villager crop farm, animal breeder, hoglin farm, or golden-carrot trade loop.
why_players_feel_forced: Every player needs food, but the most efficient option is often a farm that runs while the player does something else. Matcha can also change hunger and regeneration globally.
matcha_behavior: Observed Hunger scoreboard and tick-time hunger effects, with natural regeneration disabled. Matcha also has 128 food recipes and effect-bearing foods such as curry and ramen. Classification marks hunger, healing, and food effects as overrides. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/scoreboards.json, functions.json, recipes.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv. Final runtime amounts are UNKNOWN. Check hunger, healing, effect stacking, and restart traces.
active_route: Hunting, fishing, farming, cooking, and ordinary vanilla food remain viable and understandable.
civic_route: Communal kitchens, pantries, and settlement meals turn surplus into useful shared stock.
technical_route: Animal, crop, and cooking automation remain first-class with real feed, space, time, and bounded effect output.
trade_route: Cooked food, preserved meals, and ingredients can be sold or shipped with trait and freshness labels.
discovery_route: Regional ingredients and preparation discoveries can add knowledge without making ordinary food unusable.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive food and effect production at storage, spoilage, or demand. Effects need intensity and duration caps.
nerf_needed: Do not nerf food farms before preservation, cooking, and ordinary-food routes work. Matcha's global hunger and healing overrides need explicit compatibility decisions.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla food and Matcha recipes are present. Cooking and climate mods are provisional for 26.2.
custom_work_required: Own stable food traits, preservation, and effect stacking while treating unknown modded food as ordinary food.
open_questions: Which hunger and effect pressures are intentional, and can every food rule be explained in the Field Guide?

current_vanilla_pressure: Crops supply food, breeding, dyes, trading, and regional ingredients. Growth is passive but usually requires land, water, and repeated harvest handling.
common_optimal_farm: Villager crop farm, bonemeal loop, or large automated planting and harvesting system.
why_players_feel_forced: Crops are renewable but time-gated, and one efficient farm can supply both food and emeralds, making farming infrastructure feel compulsory.
matcha_behavior: Observed recipe-unlock advancements for crops, extensive farmer trade records, and crop references in loot and assets. No crop-growth or climate rule is established by the static audit. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/advancements.json, registry-data.json, loot-tables.json. Growth behaviour is UNKNOWN.
active_route: Manual gardens, mixed farms, fishing, and foraging remain valid.
civic_route: A greenhouse, seed library, or communal farm can turn discovered crops into reliable local supply.
technical_route: Irrigation, planting, and harvesting automation may scale with land, water, energy, and output handling.
trade_route: Seeds and produce can be sold or imported after the crop is known.
discovery_route: First regional discovery or sample establishes knowledge; cultivation should follow rather than erase the discovery.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive harvest by storage and demand, with diminishing value after buffers fill.
nerf_needed: No crop-growth nerf before preservation, trade, and cultivation alternatives are usable. Avoid making hunger harder to justify farming changes.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla farming, Matcha farmer trades, and recipe unlocks are present. Climate and farming mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Define regional discovery, climate adapters, and cross-mod crop tags without adding a one-off integration per crop.
open_questions: Which crops should be regionally distinctive, and what is the minimum discovery proof before home cultivation?

current_vanilla_pressure: Dyes support building palettes, banners, concrete, candles, and maps. Some colours require awkward mobs or rare flowers.
common_optimal_farm: Flower farm, squid or glow-squid farm, wither-rose farm, or bone-meal duplication.
why_players_feel_forced: A large build may need thousands of one colour, and the technically efficient source can require a specialised farm that has little to do with building.
matcha_behavior: Observed alternate dye recipes and flower-cloning recipe unlocks after bonemeal, plus dye references in loot. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, advancements.json, loot-tables.json. No dye-farm balance rule is established; farm behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check flower, ink, and wither-rose farm traces.
active_route: Flower gathering, ink collection, and landscape stewardship remain valid.
civic_route: A dyeworks or gardener can supply declared palette orders from real plants or mob inputs.
technical_route: Flower and mob farms remain first-class with bounded output and no infinite structure bonuses.
trade_route: Dyes and finished coloured blocks can be traded or shipped.
discovery_route: A first biome, flower, or regional colour discovery can widen the palette without prescribing one style.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Saturate passive dye at storage or project demand, especially with wither-rose and ink farms.
nerf_needed: No dye-farm nerf before dyeworks, palette substitution, and trade are usable. Preserve rare colour routes for specialists.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla dye routes and Matcha alternate recipes are present. Dyeworks and decorative mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Connect blueprint palette categories to functional equivalence, not to a required aesthetic or a generic rarity tier.
open_questions: How can rare dyes remain interesting without making a player's chosen architectural style expensive by fiat?

current_vanilla_pressure: Villagers are physically costly to breed, transport, protect, and house, but population often becomes a production input rather than a community.
common_optimal_farm: Villager breeder, curing loop, transport rail, and trading hall.
why_players_feel_forced: Many renewable resources depend on villagers, so players build a population machine and accept cramped halls even when they dislike that playstyle.
matcha_behavior: Observed villager-friend tags, environmental village functions, and many trade records, but no Matcha career, rank, or knowledge field. The reviewed classification is undecided with high persistence and multiplayer risk. Runtime population and mortality behaviour are UNKNOWN. Check breeding, unloading, rejoin, and two-player traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/tags.json, functions.json, registry-data.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv.
active_route: Find, transport, and care for a small number of villagers through ordinary play, with survival protection and meaningful relationships.
civic_route: Homes, schools, workplaces, and settlements give population a civic purpose beyond vending offers.
technical_route: Automation may handle bounded breeding, transport, and schedules, but unloaded settlements use abstract simulation and never random off-screen death.
trade_route: A steward can hire or relocate professionals, with solo access and explicit capacity.
discovery_route: Meeting a village, mentor, or regional practice can reveal a career without requiring a hall.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap breeding and service capacity by housing, food, care, and settlement demand rather than by arbitrary global scarcity.
nerf_needed: Do not nerf breeders or halls before professional training, workshops, and trade alternatives work. First remove the forced dependency, not the player's chosen farm.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla villagers and Matcha trade records are present. Career and settlement mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Create persistent career and mortality boundaries with versioned records, bounded simulation, and no player-proximity credit.
open_questions: What population size makes a settlement feel alive while preventing villagers from becoming a pure throughput multiplier?

current_vanilla_pressure: Villager trades provide renewable tools, books, food, blocks, and emeralds. Discounts and restocks make halls exceptionally efficient.
common_optimal_farm: Trading hall with curing discounts, profession control, and restock infrastructure.
why_players_feel_forced: A player can replace mining, farming, and exploration with a compact hall that supplies too many unrelated capabilities at once.
matcha_behavior: Observed 290 registry-data records and trade sets including high-volume offers such as one emerald for 64 comparators and cartographer exploration maps. Trade-set loading, restock, discounts, and per-villager scope are explicitly UNKNOWN in the audit. Check offer creation, restock, unload, and ordinary-vanilla traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/registry-data.json, tags.json, cross-references.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv.
active_route: Trading remains a useful active negotiation and service, not the only way to get books or materials.
civic_route: Professionals operate from real workplaces and settlement demand, with rest, capacity, and knowledge that can be taught.
technical_route: Technical item supply can produce components directly, so trade is not the mandatory entrance to redstone or building.
trade_route: Trade is a first-class route with willingness-to-pay, finite offers, visible restock, and no requirement for another player.
discovery_route: Cartographers and mentors can reveal maps, techniques, and broad leads rather than exact artifact checklists.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive trade output through offer uses, storage, demand, and service capacity. AFKing beside a hall should saturate.
nerf_needed: No blanket villager-trade nerf before direct production, professional training, and commerce alternatives work. Matcha trade loading needs a separate compatibility decision.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla trading and Matcha trade definitions are present. Villager and economy mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Own stable offer identity, restock, discounts, and migration without copying Matcha private paths into core systems.
open_questions: Which offers are genuinely specialist services, and which cross-domain offers recreate the exact checklist dominance this matrix is meant to remove?

current_vanilla_pressure: Emeralds are both a material and a villager currency. A separate transferable purse must avoid inventory clutter and duplication.
common_optimal_farm: Villager trading, raid farm, crop farm, or paper/book loop.
why_players_feel_forced: Currency farming can become the universal prerequisite for maps, gear, blocks, and services, while physical emerald storage creates inventory pressure.
matcha_behavior: Observed Obol tutorial and recipe-unlock advancements trigger on minecraft:emerald, and an abbey grave loot table includes emerald. No purse, balance scoreboard, deposit, withdrawal, transfer, or overflow guard was observed. Currency semantics beyond these observations are UNKNOWN. Check purse, drop, transfer, overflow, and ordinary-emerald traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/advancements.json, loot-tables.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv.
active_route: Treasure, commissions, and direct work can earn physical currency without requiring a raid farm.
civic_route: A settlement treasury, purse, or ledger can make currency useful without consuming many inventory slots.
technical_route: Automated currency production remains valid when its inputs, offers, storage, and demand are bounded.
trade_route: Merchants, shops, and freight services can accept a hybrid physical and purse balance with atomic transfers.
discovery_route: Finding the first currency practice or trade region can explain value without making every discovery a payment gate.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap balances or passive earnings through demand, offer capacity, and overflow-safe storage. Do not let AFK currency accumulate without a sink.
nerf_needed: Do not nerf raid or trade currency before a usable hybrid Obol route exists. Preserve ordinary emeralds until exact identity is proven.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla emeralds and Matcha emerald-based records are present. Purse and economy support are custom and provisional.
custom_work_required: Implement a versioned hybrid currency boundary, exact Matcha translation, and duplication-safe purse/ItemStack transfers.
open_questions: What is the stable distinction between an ordinary emerald, a physical Obol, and a purse balance?

current_vanilla_pressure: Shulker boxes solve portable bulk storage and are usually delayed behind End exploration. Their nesting and duplication risks are structural.
common_optimal_farm: End-city shulker hunting, shulker farm, or a looting and transport loop.
why_players_feel_forced: Players rush the End primarily for inventory capacity, then use boxes to make every other farm and expedition easier.
matcha_behavior: Reviewed classification keeps Matcha shulker behaviour provisionally. The shulker entity loot table returns a shulker box through killed-by-player and looting-sensitive branches; silk_touch and sack recipes also exist. No Matcha nesting hook was observed. Runtime nesting behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check every relevant container, shulker contents, and cache movement trace. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/loot-tables.json, recipes.json, assets.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv.
active_route: A bounded early Traveler's Cache handles essentials, while ordinary shulkers remain a valid later bulk-storage route.
civic_route: Warehouses and local search reduce the need to carry every item and give shulkers a civic role as physical containers.
technical_route: Storage automation can index and move physical boxes but must reject recursive container nesting and preserve revisions.
trade_route: Shulkers and warehouse services can be bought or commissioned after discovery without making an End rush mandatory.
discovery_route: End discovery remains valuable for first access and knowledge, but basic building and food do not depend on it.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap portable capacity through slot rules and no nesting. Passive shulker production should saturate at demand and storage.
nerf_needed: Do not remove or heavily delay shulkers before early portable storage and local warehouse search exist. Fix the rush by adding alternatives, not by making inventory worse.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla shulker behaviour and Matcha sack/silk-touch recipes are present. Storage mods are provisional for 26.2.
custom_work_required: Preserve physical ItemStack source-of-truth, versioned cache contents, and safe movement across death, trade, and dimensions.
open_questions: What is the earliest useful Cache size that relieves inventory pressure without making shulker boxes irrelevant?

current_vanilla_pressure: Bones, string, rotten flesh, arrows, leather, feathers, rare drops, and special materials feed many unrelated systems. General mob farms aggregate all of them.
common_optimal_farm: General hostile mob farm, dungeon spawner, raid farm, or targeted witch/guardian/slime farm.
why_players_feel_forced: A single farm replaces hunting, exploration, and several regional trips, so players build it even when they enjoy the active activities it replaces.
matcha_behavior: Static source sets drop_chances to zero for mundane hostiles, zombified piglins, and piglins in difficulty functions, while loot tables use killed-by-player, looting, random chance, and set-count rules. No runtime final drop trace exists; final drop behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check direct, indirect, automated, and looting traces. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/functions.json, loot-tables.json, docs/matcha-audit/system-classification.csv.
active_route: Hunting, structures, caves, fishing, and targeted expeditions remain meaningful sources.
civic_route: Butchers, fletchers, alchemists, and settlement works can turn declared drops into services or project stock.
technical_route: General and targeted farms remain first-class, but spawn rates, storage, and output demand must be bounded. Spawners should not be silently replaced.
trade_route: Drops can be traded or shipped from regions where the relevant mob or habitat is known.
discovery_route: First encounters teach habitats and uses without forcing repeat dungeon clearing for basic materials.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive drop output by storage, recipes, and live demand. AFK accumulation should diminish after buffers fill.
nerf_needed: No broad mob-farm nerf before active, civic, and trade routes cover ordinary needs. Resolve Matcha drop-chance overrides with runtime tests rather than assumptions.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla farms and Matcha spawn/loot modifications are present. Mob-management mods are provisional.
custom_work_required: Own exact drop identity, automation compatibility, difficulty behaviour, and unknown-item preservation behind the adapter.
open_questions: Which drops need regional or discovery context, and which should remain ordinary renewable materials?

current_vanilla_pressure: Redstone dust, repeaters, comparators, pistons, observers, rails, and copper wiring form a dependency web. A few farms supply most inputs.
common_optimal_farm: Witch/redstone farm, iron and gold farms, slime farm, quartz mining, and villager trading hall.
why_players_feel_forced: Technical builds are the main way to automate anything, but their inputs are cross-coupled with the same farms that the modpack is trying to make optional.
matcha_behavior: Observed 25 redstone-related recipes, including copper wire, redstone block, lamps, targets, and copper components. Matcha trade records include high-volume comparator offers. Evidence: generated/matcha/1.12/recipes.json, registry-data.json, advancements.json, cross-references.json. No global redstone-farm rule is established; farm behaviour is UNKNOWN. Check witch, component, and trade-output traces.
active_route: Manual redstone and small circuits remain valid for local automation and experimentation.
civic_route: A redstone works, railworks, or technical guild can supply declared components for civic projects.
technical_route: Engineering remains first-class and may reach high throughput with real iron, gold, quartz, slime, energy, design, and output handling.
trade_route: Components can be traded, commissioned, or shipped, reducing the need to personally own every source farm.
discovery_route: Discovering a component relationship or a regional technical practice can teach possibilities without requiring a full factory.
passive_output_cap_needed: Yes. Cap passive component output by storage, project demand, and offer capacity. Do not cap active design work itself.
nerf_needed: No blanket redstone nerf. First add direct crafting, trade, and civic works, then measure whether a specific farm still invalidates alternatives.
existing_mod_support: Vanilla redstone and Matcha copper/redstone recipes and trades are present. Tech mods are provisional for 26.2.
custom_work_required: Define cross-mod tags and demand accounting without replacing the player's own redstone designs or making technical play second-class.
open_questions: Which component shortages are genuine design friction, and which are only symptoms of iron, gold, slime, quartz, or villager dominance?
